Last Friday (the 21st), during the verdict in the Hong Kong Alliance case, police took a woman who was queuing to attend the hearing into a police vehicle in the early morning. In response to inquiries, police said the woman was arrested on three charges: "behaving in a disorderly manner in a public place", "resisting or intentionally obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty", and "with seditious intent".

At around 5 a.m. last Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During that time, a plainclothes officer pointed at a woman in the queue, saying her "clothing was suspected to carry seditious intent", and took her away in a police vehicle. While officers were taking the woman away, multiple officers repeatedly instructed reporters to leave, saying "take you to the press area", and pulled the orange cordon towards Nga Yuk Street. After the woman boarded the police vehicle, they retracted the cordon. On the same day, a "trial observer" queuing near the woman said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese text printed on it.

"Collective" inquired with police about the reason the woman was taken away, and whether charges had been laid. Police replied this morning (the 24th) that during a security operation in the West Kowloon Courts area on 21 August, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "behaving in a disorderly manner in a public place", "resisting or intentionally obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty", and "with seditious intent", and is being detained for investigation.
